insights.concise_text: Morphological segmentation reduced the Tamil target vocabulary from 340,325 words to 41,906 morphs, allowing RNNMorph to accommodate 100% of English and Tamil words while RNNSearch used only 44% Tamil and 74% English vocabulary.

triple.subject: morphological segmentation
triple.object: 100% vocabulary coverage in RNNMorph versus 44% Tamil and 74% English in RNNSearch

insights.concise_text: The RNNMorph model’s reduced target vocabulary from 340,325 words to 41,906 morphs is linked to earlier perplexity saturation and consistently better perplexity values than RNNSearch + Word2Vec.

triple.subject: reduced target vocabulary from 340,325 words to 41,906 morphs
triple.object: earlier perplexity saturation and consistently better perplexity values in RNNMorph

insights.concise_text: Human evaluation was used to check whether the BLEU increase from morphological segmentation reflected actual translation performance, and ranking Kappa co-efficient 0.573 for RNNMorph exceeded 0.410 for RNNSearch+Word2Vec.

triple.subject: human evaluation
triple.object: RNNMorph producing better results than RNNSearch + Word2Vec

insights.concise_text: The paper’s trade-off between domain specificity and corpus size was implemented by combining EnTam v2, tourism, and AU-KBC corpora into 197,792 sentences from various domains.

triple.subject: trade-off between domain specificity and size of the corpus
triple.object: a 197,792-sentence combination of corpora from various domains

insights.concise_text: The extra monolingual Tamil corpus used for word2vec embedding and the phrase-based SMT language model supplied the larger corpus that gave word vectors more contextual richness.

triple.subject: extra monolingual Tamil corpus
triple.object: more contextual richness for word2vec vectors

insights.concise_text: The Bahdanau et al. Bahdanau2014 translation model used here addresses the static context vector drawback of earlier RNN Encoder Decoder models by using attention-based selective source sentence lookup.

triple.subject: Bahdanau et al. Bahdanau2014 model
triple.object: earlier RNN Encoder Decoder models with attention-based selective source sentence lookup

insights.concise_text: Global attention was preferred because English and Tamil structural discordance made local monotonic lookup impractical, while the Bahdanau et al. Bahdanau2014 attention mechanism enabled selective source sentence lookup.

triple.subject: structural discordance between English and Tamil sentences
triple.object: preference for global attention over local attention

insights.concise_text: Morphological segmentation decreased the target vocabulary from 340,325 to 41,906 and reduced unknown tokens, but increased morphs per sentence and is linked to repeated phrases in RNNMorph translations.

triple.subject: morphological segmentation
triple.object: RNNMorph translations through repeated phrases despite reduced unknown tokens

insights.concise_text: The model implemented in this paper uses source-side morphological segmentation but lacks target side morphological agglutination, so a morphological generator is essential because translation output units cannot be morphemes.

triple.subject: source-side morphological segmentation without target side morphological agglutination
triple.object: a morphological generator

insights.concise_text: The 2GB NVIDIA GeForce GT 650M card with 384 cores constrained hidden layer size and batch size, motivating the future-work claim that a better GPU would improve their allocation.

triple.subject: 2GB NVIDIA GeForce GT 650M card with 384 cores
triple.object: hidden layer sizes and batch sizes
